About

About this site

What this site is

An onboarding guide and reference for CPDSE-teachers. The Start page explains why CPDSE works from three reference models and how they fit together. The explorers for Where, What and How let you look up every substep, competency and practice, and follow the links between them.

The site is not yet linked from the main cpdse.dk navigation and asks search engines not to index it.

Status of the content

The Pharma Value Chain (v0.8.0) and the Pedagogic Practices (v0.1.1) are marked in their source documents as AI-drafted and pending review, so every page for those two models carries a draft badge. The PDS Competence Model has no version number; this site shows the date it last changed (2026-07-24).

The connections between the value chain and the competence model come only from the tool crosswalk (151 links). CPDSE deliberately does not keep a fixed map from substeps to competencies: targets are set for each course or workshop.

The two worked examples use real courses. The People Development workshop, the starting levels, the targets and the session designs are illustrative.

How it is built

Every page is generated by a script in the website repository from the CPDSE reference-models repository at commit 9077859 (2026-08-31). Page copy like this is written by hand; model content is read from the source documents and vocabulary files, so the site changes when the models change and the site is rebuilt.

Glossary

CPDSE-teacher
A member of CPDSE staff who designs or runs courses and workshops with partners.
PDS
Pharmaceutical Data Science, as in the PDS Competence Model.
Curriculum course
A course in a university programme, such as SDU's BSc Pharmacy or UCPH's MSc Pharmaceutical Sciences, that CPDSE helps upgrade or create.
People Development
CPDSE's learning offer for people already in post: researchers, educators and technical or administrative staff. It includes the one-hour FrAIday Bar, the informal Vibe Café and tailored workshops for a group.
Step
One of the three top-level parts of the Pharma Value Chain: Pre-clinical, Clinical development and On-market.
Substep
One of the 14 parts of the Pharma Value Chain, such as Lead Identification. Each belongs to one step.
Domain
One of the 7 top-level areas of the PDS Competence Model, such as Mathematics & Statistics.
Sub-area
A group of related competencies inside a domain of the PDS Competence Model, such as Statistics.
Competency
One specific capability inside a sub-area, such as Hypothesis testing, described at five levels.
Level
How well someone does a competency, from L1 Awareness to L5 Expertise.
Target working level
L3 Proficiency: independently delivering usable work on standard pharma problems. Nobody is expected to reach it in every competency.
Target
The level a course or workshop aims to bring people to for a chosen competency.
Crosswalk
The list that links each tool or method in the value chain to a substep and a competence sub-area.
Tool-based link
A connection between a substep and a competence sub-area that exists because both use the same tool or method in the crosswalk. It shows overlap, not a requirement.
Session
One whole teaching event, such as a two-hour class or a half-day workshop, planned as a 4Cs sequence.
Block
One timed part of a session. Each block does the job of one of the 4Cs.
4Cs
Connections, Concepts, Concrete Practice, Conclusions: Sharon Bowman's four-part plan for any session.
Six Trumps
Six brain-based rules of thumb from Sharon Bowman, such as 'talking trumps listening', used to check each block.
Illustrative
Invented for teaching purposes. The levels and designs in the examples are not assessments of real people or courses.
Draft
The source document is marked as AI-drafted and still pending review by CPDSE.
